2016.emphasis_summary: The human-capital excerpt is a shareholder proposal for an employment diversity report (women 47.8% of the workforce but 29.2% of executives and managers) that the board opposes by citing associate resource groups and a careers diversity microsite, while the environment excerpt is a strategy narrative built on customer experience, product authority and capital allocation.
2016.notable_shifts: First available year in sample; no prior-year comparison.

2017.emphasis_summary: The human-capital excerpt repeats the employment diversity report proposal with updated figures (women 29.73% of executives and managers), and the environment excerpt is a shareholder proposal touching on climate change and political candidate support.
2017.notable_shifts: The environment excerpt switches from the 2016 strategy narrative to a shareholder proposal on climate change and political engagement, while the executive-level representation figures tick up (women 29.2% to 29.73%; the other group 12.2% to 14.01%).

2018.emphasis_summary: The human-capital excerpt keeps the diversity-report proposal with the same representation figures as 2017, and the environment excerpt is a shareholder proposal on executive pay recoupment (clawback) policies tied to sustainable value creation.
2018.notable_shifts: Human-capital figures are unchanged from 2017, while the environment excerpt moves from a climate and political-spending proposal to a clawback proposal that ties executive pay to long-term value.

2019.emphasis_summary: The human-capital excerpt highlights the February 2019 cut in the special-meeting threshold from 25% to 15% and an updated compensation clawback policy, and the environment excerpt describes an ESG engagement program with institutional shareholders that produced governance changes.
2019.notable_shifts: Governance changes now carry the human-capital excerpt, and the environment excerpt reframes sustainability as an ESG engagement dialogue, replacing the 2018 clawback-proposal text.

2020.emphasis_summary: The environment excerpt recounts ESG engagement outcomes with institutional investors, and the human-capital excerpt restates the special-meeting threshold and clawback changes as completed prior-year actions.
2020.notable_shifts: The structure is nearly unchanged from 2019, but the governance changes are now described as outcomes of completed engagement rather than as new actions.

2021.emphasis_summary: The diversity excerpt is the first substantive DEI section in the HD series, describing the enhanced Office of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion and expanded community support, while the human-capital excerpt highlights SASB- and TCFD-aligned disclosure and expanded government-relations reporting.
2021.notable_shifts: The diversity section is populated for the first time, and the human-capital excerpt moves from rebutting an EEO proposal to climate-framework disclosure commitments.

2022.emphasis_summary: The excerpts describe ESG engagement outreach to institutional investors and new climate-related goals, with the human-capital excerpt citing the consolidated EEO-1 report and the 2021 ESG Report.
2022.notable_shifts: Climate-related goals and EEO-1 workforce reporting move into the human-capital excerpt, and the environment excerpt adds more explicit ESG-engagement language.

2023.emphasis_summary: The human-capital excerpt covers the 2022 CEO transition from Craig Menear to Ted Decker, and the diversity excerpt adds pay-equity disclosures made in response to investor engagement.
2023.notable_shifts: Climate-goal framing gives way to leadership-succession and pay-equity content, shifting the emphasis from ESG engagement to workforce pay and executive transition.

2024.emphasis_summary: The excerpts are a list of 2024 shareholder proposals on biodiversity impact, clawback policy and civil liberties, each recommended against, plus a note on structural leadership changes that elevated Ann-Marie Campbell to senior executive vice president.
2024.notable_shifts: The pay-equity and CEO-transition disclosures from 2023 give way to a catalogue of shareholder proposals with board recommendations, and the environment content turns to strategic leadership structure.
